title: The 6 Rs Migration Strategy
description: Learn the 6 Rs migration strategy framework — Rehost, Replatform, Repurchase, Refactor, Retire, and Retain.

data.text: The **6 Rs** is a framework from AWS that helps you decide how to migrate each application. Each R represents a different approach, from simple 'lift and shift' to complete rebuilding.

rows: Lift and shift — move as-is to the cloud
Lift and optimize — change platform (e.g., RDS instead of self-managed DB)
Switch to a cloud-native alternative (e.g., SaaS)
Turn off applications you no longer need
Keep on-premises — do not migrate yet

data.title: When to Use Each Strategy
items: **Rehost** — quick cloud adoption, legacy apps, time-constrained projects
**Replatform** — reduce management overhead without changing code
**Refactor** — long-term agility, need for serverless or microservices
**Retire** — eliminate waste and reduce attack surface
**Retain** — compliance reasons, mainframes, or apps not ready

data.title: A Typical Migration Plan
items: Assess each application against the 6 Rs
Build a landing zone (networking, IAM, security)
Migrate in waves, starting with low-risk apps
Optimize costs and performance after migration

data.title: Planning Tip
data.text: Most organizations start with Rehost to move quickly, then Replatform and Refactor over time. This 'crawl, walk, run' approach reduces risk.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: The 6 Rs help you choose the right migration strategy
Rehost is fastest but least optimized
Refactor delivers the most cloud benefits but takes the longest
Always retire what you no longer need
